strings.d1.s0.name: Edinburgh Castle
strings.d1.s0.tips: A castle on a volcanic rock: see the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny and the 13:00 gun firing. Book a timed slot online (they sell out).
strings.d1.s1.name: Royal Mile
strings.d1.s1.tips: 1.6 km from the castle to Holyrood. Take in St Giles' Cathedral (Thistle Chapel), the closes (narrow alleys) and the Mary King's Close tour.
strings.d1.s2.name: Deacon Brodie's Tavern
strings.d1.s2.tips: Named after the thieving councillor who inspired Dr Jekyll. Try haggis, neeps and tatties.
strings.d1.s3.name: The Real Mary King's Close
strings.d1.s3.tips: 17th-century streets buried beneath the road above; plague history. Book ahead.
strings.d1.s4.name: The Scotch Whisky Experience
strings.d1.s4.tips: A barrel ride and a tasting, with a collection of 3,000 bottles. On Castlehill.
strings.d1.b0.name: Oink
strings.d1.b0.tips: Hog roast sandwiches; expect a queue.
strings.d1.b1.name: Camera Obscura
strings.d1.b1.tips: An illusion tower dating from 1835. An alternative to Mary King's Close, good with children.
strings.d2.s0.name: Arthur's Seat
strings.d2.s0.tips: An extinct volcano, 251 m high. 45 minutes from Holyrood Park, with panoramic views over the city and the Firth of Forth. It's windy.
strings.d2.s1.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
strings.d2.s1.tips: The monarch's residence in Scotland. See Mary Queen of Scots' rooms and the ruined abbey.
strings.d2.s2.name: The Sheep Heid Inn
strings.d2.s2.tips: Said to be Scotland's oldest pub, dating from 1360 (royalty visited). It has a skittles alley and a village setting in Duddingston.
strings.d2.s3.name: Calton Hill
strings.d2.s3.tips: Home to the National Monument (an unfinished Parthenon) and the Nelson Monument. The best postcard view of the city, especially at sunset.
strings.d2.s4.name: Dean Village
strings.d2.s4.tips: A medieval mill village on the Water of Leith, a fairytale corner in the middle of the city.
strings.d2.b0.name: Dynamic Earth
strings.d2.b0.tips: A science centre telling the story of the planet. An alternative to Holyrood, good with children.
strings.d2.b1.name: Holyrood 9A
strings.d2.b1.tips: Burgers and craft beer, just below the Royal Mile.
strings.d3.s0.name: National Gallery of Scotland
strings.d3.s0.tips: Free, on the Mound. See Titian, Raeburn's The Skating Minister and Monarch of the Glen.
strings.d3.s1.name: Princes Street Gardens and Scott Monument
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Gothic rocket-shaped monument with 287 steps. The gardens have castle views and a floral clock.
strings.d3.s2.name: Stockbridge Market and Circus Lane
strings.d3.s2.tips: The market runs on Sundays. Circus Lane is a flower-lined back street, very Instagrammable.
strings.d3.s3.name: The Scran and Scallie
strings.d3.s3.tips: Tom Kitchin's gastropub in Stockbridge, serving Scottish ingredients.
strings.d3.s4.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
strings.d3.s4.tips: A botanic garden since 1670. The glasshouses are paid; Inverleith Hill has castle views.
strings.d3.b0.name: Scottish National Portrait Gallery
strings.d3.b0.tips: A neo-Gothic red building. Free entry, with portraits of Mary Stuart.
strings.d3.b1.name: The Pantry
strings.d3.b1.tips: Brunch in Stockbridge; expect a queue.
strings.d4.s0.name: Rosslyn Chapel
strings.d4.s0.tips: The 1446 chapel from The Da Vinci Code. See the Apprentice Pillar and hundreds of carvings. Take the 37 bus, 40 minutes.
strings.d4.s1.name: Roslin Glen
strings.d4.s1.tips: A walk through the stream valley below the chapel, with a ruined castle.
strings.d4.s2.name: The Original Rosslyn Inn
strings.d4.s2.tips: A village inn; lunch at the pub.
strings.d4.s3.name: Pentland Hills, Flotterstone
strings.d4.s3.tips: Winter hills. The Hillend artificial ski slope is an alternative.
strings.d4.b0.name: Craigmillar Castle
strings.d4.b0.tips: A ruined castle where Mary Stuart took refuge. Inside the city, an alternative to the Pentlands.
strings.d4.b1.name: Flotterstone Inn
strings.d4.b1.tips: A pub at the entrance to the Pentlands.
strings.d5.s0.name: Stirling Castle
strings.d5.s0.tips: 50 minutes by train. The castle of the Scottish kings, with the Great Hall and views of the Wallace Monument.
strings.d5.s1.name: National Wallace Monument
strings.d5.s1.tips: The 67 m tower tied to Braveheart and the 1297 Battle of Stirling Bridge. 246 steps.
strings.d5.s2.name: Stirling Old Town lunch
strings.d5.s2.tips: A café next to the Old Town Jail; try Cullen skink (smoked haddock soup).
strings.d5.s3.name: Balloch, Loch Lomond
strings.d5.s3.tips: The loch shore in winter. Luss village is reachable by car.
strings.d5.s4.name: Luss
strings.d5.s4.tips: A stone village on the loch shore. The pier at sunset (by tour or car).
strings.d5.b0.name: Doune Castle
strings.d5.b0.tips: The Monty Python and Outlander castle. An alternative to the Wallace Monument (by car).
strings.d5.b1.name: The Portcullis
strings.d5.b1.tips: A pub at the castle gate.
strings.d6.s0.name: Royal Yacht Britannia
strings.d6.s0.tips: The Queen's yacht from 1953 to 1997, moored at Ocean Terminal in Leith. Audio guide included.
strings.d6.s1.name: The Shore, Leith
strings.d6.s1.tips: The old harbour and Trainspotting's neighbourhood, with Michelin-starred restaurants.
strings.d6.s2.name: Fishers in Leith
strings.d6.s2.tips: Seafood in a harbour tower, open since 1991.
strings.d6.s3.name: Water of Leith Walkway
strings.d6.s3.tips: A 5 km riverside path from Leith to Dean Village, with Antony Gormley statues in the water.
strings.d6.s4.name: Surgeons' Hall Museums
strings.d6.s4.tips: A surgical museum covering the body snatchers Burke and Hare. Not for the faint-hearted.
strings.d6.b0.name: The Kitchin
strings.d6.b0.tips: Michelin-starred. Book the lunch menu ahead.
strings.d6.b1.name: Portobello Beach
strings.d6.b1.tips: A city beach with a Victorian promenade. An alternative to Leith.
strings.d7.s0.name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
strings.d7.s0.tips: Home to the Greyfriars Bobby dog statue. Harry Potter names appear on gravestones (Tom Riddle).
strings.d7.s1.name: The Elephant House
strings.d7.s1.tips: Breakfast at the café where Rowling wrote (reopened). The back room has castle views.
strings.d7.s2.name: National Museum of Scotland
strings.d7.s2.tips: See Dolly the sheep and the Lewis Chessmen. Free entry, with a rooftop terrace.
strings.d7.s3.name: Waverley Station
strings.d7.s3.tips: Take the tram to the airport, 35 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Mums Great Comfort Food
strings.d7.b0.tips: On Forrest Road; sausages and mash.
strings.d7.b1.name: Grassmarket
strings.d7.b1.tips: A Saturday farmers' and crafts market.
strings.note0: A Lothian bus day ticket costs 5.50 GBP (via the app); the airport tram costs 7 GBP. Take the train to Stirling and Loch Lomond, and the 37 bus to Rosslyn. The city is hilly but walkable.
strings.note1: December brings Hogmanay (the New Year street party, with a torchlit procession on 30 December) and the Christmas market. Winter is 3-7°C, windy and rainy, and it gets dark by 15:30. May is ideal.
strings.note2: The castle costs 20 GBP and must be booked online. Museums (National, Galleries) are FREE. Pub lunch is 15-20 GBP, a whisky tasting 25 GBP; tip 10%.
strings.note3: Try haggis, Cullen skink, Scotch pie, cranachan and Irn-Bru. For whisky, Islay is smoky and Speyside is sweet.
strings.note4: The weather can turn through four seasons in an hour: bring a rain jacket and layers. The wind is harsh on Calton Hill and Arthur's Seat.
strings.note5: Harry Potter spots: Victoria Street, Greyfriars, the Elephant House and the Balmoral Hotel's Room 552.
